title: Jeannine M NDE 6580
content: I was spending a weekend at the beach in Sète (near Spain on the Med), and I was in a restaurant with my husband, my son and my mother. My mother asked me to go with her to the toilets. I crossed the dining room and started to feel unwell. We went outside and I waited for her there. There was a man waiting there. As I was told later, it was a man who told my husband and my mother that I had fainted. I just felt myself leaving my body through the top of my head, (with some difficulty) then finding myself out of it. That is, free. Then I said to myself, ‘I'm dead. I'm going to be buried here in Sète, like Paul Valéry and Georges Brassens’ (the latter was still alive, but was buried in Sète after he died). I was all right, observing the cement paving stones on the terrace, which seemed wonderful to me, as did the sea and the sand. Suddenly I was projected towards a being of light who was not visible (there was no tunnel). He asked me (without a voice, by a kind of telepathy) if I accepted my death. I replied that my mother and my son still needed me. Then he kind of ‘smiled,’ or that's what I felt. A slightly mocking smile, which meant ‘no’. Then I began to defend myself, saying, ‘all right, then, but not here, not in Sète. People have been racist toward us here (which was true, but the fact is I did not want my family to bear the burden of transporting my body to Toulouse where we lived). How disappointed, yet how generous he was. Because this was my choice, he said, ‘All right, but in that case,’ and there followed a promise whose nature I did not understand. Then I fell back into my body, and there I found my family who were in a state of anxiety. We left the restaurant and returned to Toulouse where I began to regret my decision. I got dressed and crossed my hands, awaiting a death, which did not come. I have told my family all about this experience. They believe me and often talk about ‘when Jeannine died in Sète’. Later on, life has been very, very hard for me and now I know why God wanted to take me far from here. He is so good; he wanted to spare me the media persecution, which awaited me. For more than thirty years, I have been, and still am now, a laughing-stock in France and even beyond, thanks to the ‘despicable’ French media. If you don't believe me, look it up. But since then He is with me, answers my questions and loves me with an unconditional love. He and Mary help me on a daily basis. I've lost everything. My son, my grandchildren, my family and my friends, but I have gained more than anyone else can lay claim to. I have become a mystic but I still don't go to church, as I cannot trust priests or the church. They are too haughty, too wary of people like me. I write on a GOOGLE+ account but often I erase it afterwards, as it is hard to say these things, and to read them (I know that people read me, as people are up to date with my hassles with the media, who will tell you I'm crazy, of course, as this suits them).

out_of_body.vantage_other_detail: Outside on the restaurant terrace, observing the cement paving stones, the sea and the sand after leaving her body.
out_of_body.separation_sensations_other: Felt herself leaving through the top of her head 'with some difficulty,' then felt 'free.'

tunnel.movement_other_detail: Felt 'projected' toward a being of light.

arrival.other_being_detail: A 'being of light' who 'was not visible' and communicated telepathically; she perceived a slightly mocking 'smile.'

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Fainting (syncope) at a restaurant while at the beach.

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: No tunnel; telepathic question from a non-visible being of light about accepting death; negotiation about dying 'not here, not in Sète'; then return to body.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: OBE with observation of physical surroundings, then immediate projection to a non-visible being of light (no tunnel), then telepathic exchange and return.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: The being of light was described as 'not visible' and seemed to 'smile' slightly mockingly; the experiencer negotiated the location of death ('not in Sète') and mentioned a subsequent 'promise' whose nature she did not understand.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “I just felt myself leaving my body through the top of my head, (with some difficulty) then finding myself out of it. That is, free.”; “I'm dead. I'm going to be buried here in Sète...” ; “He asked me (without a voice, by a kind of telepathy) if I accepted my death.” ; “All right, but in that case,” and there followed a promise whose nature I did not understand.
